prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: ONE four-panel character-evolution comparison board for a private vocabulary-learning game, ages 10–13. Design preview, not production sprites.
Input image 1 is the CHARACTER IDENTITY reference: the existing friendly Bengal tiger, orange fur, dark black stripes, white chest and cheek fur, warm amber eyes, rounded ears, four large tiger paws and one curled striped tail. Preserve this specific recognizable tiger throughout. Input image 2 is ONLY the user-approved painterly rendering and EVOLUTION-STRENGTH reference. Do not copy its dragon anatomy, wings, antlers, teal palette, armor designs or text.
Create a polished wide landscape board with FOUR evenly separated vertical panels, plain warm ivory background, restrained thin antique-gold dividers. Four complete single tigers, one per panel, same three-quarter standing orientation facing slightly left, head gently toward viewer, same baseline and consistent light. Scale to fit the largest silhouette; every ear tip, paw, plume and tail tip must fit inside its panel with generous empty margin above and to both sides. Each bottom label EXACTLY: "STUFE 1", "STUFE 2", "STUFE 3", "STUFE 4". No other text or titles.
STUFE 1: faithfully preserve the unadorned existing Bengal tiger from image 1. Friendly calm brave expression, richly painted orange and black striped fur, white cheeks/chest, no clothes, jewelry or magic.
STUFE 2: same tiger as a jungle explorer. A clean fitted forest-green and warm-brown travel harness with small antique-gold leaf chest clasp and a small rolled-map satchel at the flank. Add restrained matching green-and-gold foreleg bands. Gear sits naturally around the upper chest and shoulders, never cuts through legs or covers the important face/stripe identity. Fur and tail still ordinary. Beautiful simple upgrade, not bulky armor.
STUFE 3: a noble ancient jungle temple guardian. A proud stronger stance, a subtly larger white cheek/chest ruff, fitted sculpted deep-jade and antique-gold shoulder/chest armor with a single warm amber sunstone, meaningful broad leaf/sun reliefs, elegant fitted foreleg guards. A modest integrated gold brow ornament above the eyes, keeping both rounded ears clearly visible. The striped body and natural curled tail remain readable; more magnificent than stage2 but still a grounded armored tiger. No antlers, horns, wings or crown floating above the head.
STUFE 4: a major mythic transformation into a legendary SOLAR JUNGLE TIGER SPIRIT, NOT merely more armor. Still recognizably the same TIGER, never a lion: rounded tiger ears, tiger face and unmistakable dark stripes retained on golden-orange fur. Noble taller posture, long flowing ivory-and-warm-gold CHEEK AND SHOULDER FUR sweeping backward into large graceful sunray-shaped tufts that dramatically change the silhouette, without a circular lion mane around the face. The long striped tail ends in a large elegant luminous golden plume instead of its ordinary rounded tip. Broad dark stripes gain subtle warm-gold luminous edges, with a few readable solar markings following the limbs. Only a restrained integrated golden sun chest emblem with amber center; less armor than stage3. Beautiful controlled light within the fur and plume, no blinding glow, no indistinct flames. Protective, wise, calm and awe-inspiring, friendly amber eyes and closed mouth. The increased silhouette, flowing fur and dramatic single tail plume must make this a true final evolution, visible even at thumbnail size. NO wings, antlers, horns, additional limbs, detached solar disc, halo, levitation or separate floating objects.
Overall palette: rich tiger orange and black, ivory white, deep forest/jade green for intermediate equipment, antique gold and warm amber; avoid default turquoise crystal dominance. Premium painterly storybook game illustration, collectible and aspirational for ages 10–13. No plastic toy look, no baby/chibi proportions, no aggression, weapons, bared teeth or horror. No scenery, no floor decoration, no smoky background, no watermarks. Every complete figure comfortably inside its own panel, labels unobstructed. Four forms of the same tiger, exactly one per panel.
